title: RE William G. Mitchell v. The Presbytery of the Ascension
disposition_detail: The judgment sustaining Specification No. 2 was vacated and remanded for Presbytery to consider whether a new trial was warranted. The judgment sustaining Specification No. 6 was reversed, and that specification was dismissed.
first_summary: A ruling elder appealed judgments concerning an alleged broken promise to take a sabbatical and deficient performance as Session clerk. The SJC vacated the first judgment because the pivotal email was missing from the record and remanded for consideration of a new trial. It reversed and dismissed the clerk-duty specification because the brief delay in submitting minutes did not justify judicial process. Thus, one specification remained potentially triable while the other ended.
summary: A ruling elder appealed judgments concerning an alleged broken promise to take a sabbatical and deficient performance as Session clerk. Because the pivotal email was absent from the record, the SJC vacated the sabbatical-related judgment and remanded for Presbytery only to consider whether a new trial was warranted. It reversed and dismissed the clerk-duty specification because the four-month delay in submitting minutes was attributable to the Session and did not justify a trial. Only the first specification remained potentially triable.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The heading identifies Case 2012-07 and the parties; the SJC adopted the panel decision 20–0 among votes cast (lines 13–15, 210–213; printed pp. 544, 553).
evidence_notes.dispute: The appeal challenged judgments sustaining the sabbatical-promise and clerk-duty specifications (lines 81–83, 91–101; printed pp. 548–549).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Specification 2 was vacated and remanded because its pivotal email was missing; Specification 6 was reversed and dismissed because the limited minutes delay did not warrant trial (lines 163–168, 180–209; printed pp. 552–553).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC reached no definitive conclusion on Specification 2 and directed Presbytery only to consider a new trial, with the complete email required if retried (lines 168–169; printed p. 552).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference; the opinion recounts an earlier complaint judgment only as procedural background (lines 49–53, 168).

source_limits: The supplied source contains the adopted decision but does not expressly state the post-appeal status of the previously imposed indefinite suspension; the synopsis therefore does not infer that status.
